s1.syndrome_frame: Severe, persistent, unilateral facial pain with trigeminal nerve involvement and abnormal sensations
salient_findings: Persistent severe pain on the left side of the face
Pain localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
Allodynia to cold air and hypersensitivity to touch in the affected area
key_facts: 36-year-old woman
Received third dose of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine
Pain started the day after vaccination
Pain initially affected the entire left hemiface
Pain localized to V2 and V3 distributions within days
Attacks last 4-5 seconds
Attacks triggered by jaw movement during eating or tooth brushing
Pain reaches 10/10 on a numeric pain scale
Distorted sensations in the V2 region during attacks
Sensory testing otherwise normal
No other neurological deficits
No relevant past medical or family history
Routine laboratory tests normal
RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and other infections negative
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head shows no abnormalities

per_call: Short-Lasting Unilateral Neuralgiform Headache with Conjunctival Injection and Tearing

shortlist.label: Trigeminal Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Classic presentation of severe, unilateral facial pain with trigeminal nerve involvement and trigger points

shortlist.label: SUNCT Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Short-lasting, unilateral neuralgiform headache with conjunctival injection and tearing, similar to the patient's episodic pain

shortlist.label: Trigeminal Neuropathic Pain
shortlist.why_kept: Pain characteristics and distribution consistent with neuropathic pain involving the trigeminal nerve

shortlist.label: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Although less common, could be considered due to the severe, episodic nature of the pain and potential involvement of adjacent nerves

shortlist.label: Raeder Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral facial pain with autonomic features, although the patient's presentation lacks some characteristic signs like ptosis and miosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, are classic for Trigeminal Neuralgia.

rejected.label: SUNCT Syndrome
rejected.why: SUNCT Syndrome typically involves shorter-lasting pain attacks and is often accompanied by conjunctival injection and lacrimation, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Trigeminal Neuropathic Pain
rejected.why: While the patient has pain in the trigeminal distribution, the episodic, shock-like nature of the pain is more characteristic of Trigeminal Neuralgia than neuropathic pain.

rejected.label: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia
rejected.why: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia involves pain in the distribution of the glossopharyngeal nerve, which is not the primary area of pain in this patient.

rejected.label: Raeder Syndrome
rejected.why: Raeder Syndrome involves a combination of trigeminal neuralgia and Horner's syndrome, which is not described in the vignette.
